activity_context.topic_title: Representing 3x3 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product

feedback.problem:
The system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-5y+z=1 \\ -x-3y+9z=-2 \\ 4x-7y-z=5\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & c \\ -1 & b & 9 \\ a & -7 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 \\ -1 & -3 & 9 \\ 4 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 9 \\ 4 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=4,\,b=-3,\,c=1.$
